entry.title: DeepWeave: Weaving Neural and Symbolic Evidence for ML-Based Network Intrusion Detection System
entry.summary:
Machine learning-based network intrusion detection systems can recognize complex traffic patterns, but often require substantial labelled attack data, degrade under deployment shift, and provide limited evidence for analysts. We present DeepWeave, a probabilistic neuro-symbolic Network Intrusion Detection System (NIDS) that makes logic an integral part of detection. DeepWeave automatically constructs and validates interpretable rules, represents neural predictions as probabilistic predicates, and reconciles both evidence sources through explicit coupling policies over packet-, flow-, and hybrid-views.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #ml-theory

entry.title: Locality-Controlled Out-of-Distribution Guidance for Robust Regulatory DNA Sequence Design
entry.summary:
Designing regulatory DNA sequences for targeted gene-expression control is an important challenge. Recent approaches frame this task as property-conditioned generation, where diffusion models trained on natural sequences are guided toward high predicted activity through reward-based fine-tuning or sampling-time guidance. We show that single-reward evaluation can obscure reward-hacking behavior.

Source: arXiv Quantitative Biology & Materials (q-bio, mtrl-sci) · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #ml-theory #clean-tech

entry.title: From Training Exposure to Membership Evidence: A Controlled Study of OLMo 2
entry.summary:
Whether a language model was trained on a document matters for copyright, privacy, and benchmark contamination. Yet most membership-inference (MI) evaluations on language models collect members and non-members after the fact, so success may reflect distribution shift and failure is inconclusive. We re-ran OLMo 2 1B's official 50-billion-token mid-training stage, replacing selected training chunks with documents from 7,814 pairs matched on domain and difficulty.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #llm #ml-theory

entry.title: When Is a Game a Markov Decision Process? Correspondences Between Game Theory and Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Reinforcement learning and game theory describe the same object from two sides. Game theory says what a rational outcome of a strategic interaction is; reinforcement learning says how an agent could reach one through experience. The two literatures nevertheless keep separate vocabularies for identical structures, and the treatments that bridge them present the correspondence as analogy rather than theorem.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #ml-theory #logic
